vendored CUTLASS under
3rdparty/
.
The pre-MMA E8M0 scale-fusion path has a distinct runtime path from the
standard post-MMA scale paths because it changes where MXFP4 weight scaling is
applied.
The MXFP4xFP8 weight preprocessing and dequantization strategy is based on
the Humming approach for fusing E8M0 scale offsets into the FP8 MMA operand:
https://github.com/inclusionAI/humming
Autotune now validates candidate Hopper mixed-input tactics against reference
output before using their timing result for tactic selection.
The benchmark figures above compare fused MoE or GEMM timing scopes as noted
in each plot title.

📌 Description
Adds the native
BF16
twin of the SM90 (Hopper) pull-style CuTeDSL MegaMoE
backend:
sm90_bf16_bf16_bf16_pull_cutedsl
(BF16 activations, BF16 expert
weights, BF16 output; fused NVSHMEM dispatch + FC1 + SwiGLU + FC2 + combine
in one persistent kernel, WGMMA with fp32 accumulation).  It is the kernel
team's
moe_hopper_bf16
drop vendored next to the existing FP8
moe_hopper_fp8
drop, with the same shim / backend / test / bench layering as
sm90_fp8_fp8_bf16_pull_cutedsl
.
What is in the PR:
Shim
shim/hopper_bf16.py
(
MegaMoEHopperBf16Config
/ frontend / symm
buffer /
hopper_bf16_mega_moe
),
shim/tuner_bf16.py
and
shim/autotune_bf16.py
(knob space, heuristic defaults, candidate sweep);
the knob cache is shared with FP8 under
dtype="bf16"
.
Backend
backends/mega/kernel/sm90/bf16_bf16_bf16_pull_cutedsl/
(
Sm90_Bf16_Bf16_Bf16_PullCutedsl_MegaMoeConfig
, staging = plain bf16
copy, weights = gate/up 8-row interleave + K-major relayout, no
quantization), registered in
flashinfer.moe_ep
, runtime requirements,
python -m flashinfer.moe_ep.tune --dtype sm90_bf16
.
Tests
mirroring the FP8 set one-to-one minus the FP8-only axes
(
test_sm90_pull_bf16_{config,tuner,kernel_vs_reference}.py
,
test_moe_ep_sm90_pull_bf16_mega_multirank.py
);
run_tests.sh
oracle_sm90
/
mega_sm90
now cover FP8 and BF16.
Bench
benchmarks/moe_ep/backends/mega/kernel/sm90/bench_moe_ep_sm90_bf16_pull_mega.py
(BF16 twin of the FP8 token sweep), and docs (
SKILL.md
,
TUNING.md
BF16
section with measured numbers,
moe_ep_architecture.md
,
moe_ep_runbook.md
).
Contract / differences from the FP8 backend:
hidden % 256 == 0
,
intermediate % 64 == 0
, tile K = 64 (two-byte operands: the 128-byte swizzle
atom spans 64 elements), heuristic table keyed on tokens only, no
kind
/
fp8_scale_mode
/
fp8_accum_mode
/ dequant scales /
dedup_dispatch
/
grouped_token_back
/
combine_format
knobs.
Performance
Three heuristic token sweeps with the benchmarks' default configuration
(DSV4-Pro P03 geometry: 384 experts, top-6, hidden 7168, intermediate 3072,
gate_up_clamp 10,
load_balance_mode=atomic_counter
, warmup 3 / 20 timed
iterations, 5 s cooldown per series, tokens/rank 8..32768), EP=4 on the same
4x H200 node with the SM clock locked at 1830 MHz:
torchrun --nproc_per_node=4 benchmarks/moe_ep/backends/mega/kernel/sm90/bench_moe_ep_sm90_mega.py --scale-mode both
torchrun --nproc_per_node=4 benchmarks/moe_ep/backends/mega/kernel/sm90/bench_moe_ep_sm90_bf16_pull_mega.py
Numbers are the
compute
series (bare
MegaKernelBackend.compute(output=None)
:
fused mega kernel + standalone top-k reduce, zero-copy output), slowest-rank
mean per iteration; TFLOPS = FC1+FC2 FLOPs of one rank over that time
(
2 * tokens * topk * hidden * (2I + I)
).  Each point runs the backend's
per-bucket heuristic launch config (FP8: swap-AB / non-swap M64N256 rows at
K=128; BF16: swap-AB rows at K=64).

Peak compute throughput per rank: FP8 per_tensor 994 TFLOPS, FP8 blockwise
845 TFLOPS, BF16 553 TFLOPS.
BF16 delivers
0.53x
the FP8 per_tensor TFLOPS (geomean over the 13
buckets, range 0.49-0.57x) and
0.60x
the FP8 blockwise TFLOPS (range
0.52-0.80x).  The ~0.5x against per_tensor is the expected ceiling: Hopper
BF16 WGMMA peaks at half the dense FP8 rate and the bf16 dispatch wire
carries twice the bytes per token, so both the GEMM-bound tail and the
latency/bandwidth-bound head halve.  Blockwise FP8 pays its per-block
scale handling on 1024+ tokens (non-swap M64N256 rows at 600-850 TFLOPS),
which is why BF16 closes to 0.63-0.80x there.
The FI
compute
path matches the kernel team's own BF16 harness
(
moe_hopper_bf16/run_token_sweep_benchmark.py
,
mega_us + topk_us
) on
the same node within +-2% at 512 / 2048 / 8192 / 32768 tokens (see the
BF16 section of
kernel_src/sm90/pull_style_cutedsl_megakernel/TUNING.md
).
e2e (
MoEEpLayer.forward
) adds only 16-240 µs over
compute
for BF16
(staging is a plain bf16 copy) versus 115-1100 µs for FP8 per_tensor and
170-2900 µs for FP8 blockwise (torch-composed quantization staging).

🔬 Experimental Track
This PR is
experimental
: it adds or changes code under
flashinfer/experimental/
and/or an
@flashinfer_experimental_api
. Tracking issue: #
The tracking issue names an owner, the reason for the experimental path, and a graduation plan with a target release.
Core changes are limited to a thin entry point (signature, shared validation, feature-gate check, backend selection, handoff).
Tests live in
tests/experimental/
and were validated on the intended hardware; a runnable example is included.
Nothing is registered in
flashinfer/aot.py

@flashinfer_experimental_api
or naming a backend explicitly is itself the opt-in and needs no environment variable.)

title: perf(cake_deepgemm_fp4_gemm): cooperative mbarrier initialisation on six routes, early load start on the BN224 / BN256 routes, and a cross-pass epilogue pipeline on the normal BN160 program (SM100a, SM103a; outputs bitwise unchanged)
body:
## Summary

Regenerates the native FP4 GEMM family `flashinfer.experimental.deepgemm_fp4_gemm` (public API `flashinfer.fp4_gemm.prepare_fp4_gemm`) for SM100a (B200) and
SM103a (GB300) at FlashInfer `22d60b5bb`. One exact schedule change reaches the native FP4 GEMM programs in this update. The normal BN160 program (`normal_bm128_bn160_s7`; cohort row model-fp4gemm-l2-m512, five epilogue passes) now pipelines its epilogue across passes: each store pass issues one `tcgen05.ld` batch for the next pass while the current pass converts and stores (one-pass lookahead), instead of loading, converting and storing pass by pass. The change is program-scoped (switched on for the BN160 program only in its source module); the helpers are in the sources for the other multi-pass programs but switched off there, and every other native FP4 GEMM program -- the seven others, including the two single-pass programs (swap-AB BM16 and normal BN16) -- renders byte-identical to the previous delivery on both architectures. In the paired A/B against the previous delivery the row reads 3.31 % faster on B200 (7.108 to 6.880 us; floor 1.24 %) and 2.47 % faster on GB300 (6.788 to 6.624 us; floor 1.06 %), beyond its floor in both rounds on each architecture (2 of 2 rounds per architecture), with 4 of 4 byte-identical control rows flat (two native FP4 GEMM rows and two FP8 x FP4 mixed-GEMM rows of the sibling family) on a reduced 5-row set (B200 under its A/B GPU-hour cap, GB300 on the same rows; the B200 A/B (both arms on the same GPU) ran on a node whose other seven GPUs held, by the cluster's job accounting, six one-GPU jobs of two other users throughout its 20-minute step and a one-GPU job of this user's unrelated work for that step's first eleven minutes, the GB300 A/B on an exclusive node with no other job on it by the same accounting). The content of this pull request's previous head is unchanged: cooperative mbarrier initialisation on the six swap-AB / BN16 / BN128 / BN160 routes and the early load start on the BN224 / BN256 normal routes. In the acceptance on the head of this update's readings (the Cake tree measured before this squash, whose programs this revision reproduces byte for byte; "this revision's head" below) the row reads native/source 1.0852 on B200 (6.912 us against native 7.500 us; the previous acceptance reading of this row, 1.0560 at 7.084 us; +2.77 %, beyond its 1.24 % band) and 1.0801 on GB300 (6.636 us against 7.168 us; the previous acceptance reading of this row, 1.0553 at 6.792 us; +2.35 %, beyond its 1.33 % band), 12 readings each; the seven other rows per architecture keep the previous head's readings.

This change adds no fast-math flag, approximate intrinsic, reduced accumulation precision, sampling or output-changing skip;
the pipeline changes when the epilogue loads each pass's accumulator slice from tensor memory relative to the previous pass's conversion and store, not the MMA, the accumulation order, the conversion or the store statements, so the changed program's outputs are bitwise identical to the previous delivery's (its knob arm against the knob-off base: at first launch and on replay for three input seeds in the bitwise arbiter of the tree that introduced the pipeline, which passed 54 of 54 checks per architecture across every built arm, and at first launch, on replay and after timing on the cohort seed in each of that tree's three timing processes per architecture; its cohort launcher closure among that tree's 20 matched the launcher's own N128 control program bitwise at first launch and on replay (not the knob-off base; the knob is installed process-wide in that closure, so that control was traced with the pipeline on as well, and the same row's base-arm closure matched the control with the pipeline off); the paired A/B against the previous delivery passed correctness on every row and round on both architectures; all on the tree that introduced the pipeline, carried to the head of the acceptance readings by its identity render against that tree (8 of 8 cohort rows byte-identical) and to this revision by the identity render of this change against that head (120 of 120 rendered rows per architecture), taken on an earlier squash of this change on the same Cake parent before its two formatting-only template fixes, which touch no program source); inputs, outputs and the public `prepare_fp4_gemm` signature are unchanged.

## What changed in the generated package (vs FlashInfer `22d60b5bb`)

- `csrc/experimental/deepgemm_fp4_gemm/`: 8 new programs (8 `*_kernel.cu` + 8 `*_binding.cu` with content-hashed names), 8 removed (8 kernels + 8 bindings), 0 modified in place. The family keeps its 8 programs, each re-rendered under a new content-hashed name (beyond the programs the pull request adds, against main, the package's clang-format opt-out and the shared helper `csrc/cake_device_helpers/cake_tcgen05_mma_mxf4_bs_cta2_bfa583d21358df24.cuh`, and rewrites the device preamble `cake_deepgemm_fp4_gemm_device_common.cuh` (+17 / -141: its inline helpers become 15 `#include` lines); 36 paths change against main in all (18 added, 16 removed, 2 modified; git's default rename detection pairs 15 removed program files with added ones and reports 21 files changed)); the host module's program table (`flashinfer/experimental/deepgemm_fp4_gemm/fp4_gemm.py`) is the delivered one.
- `csrc/cake_device_helpers/`: 1 new content-hashed helper header (in the helper directory the Cake export families share); the 14 helpers this family's programs include that main already carries are unchanged: the sealed run rendered its own copies of them under this family's license header and formatting, token-identical to main's files, and a content-addressed helper already in the target is never rewritten (the exporter's retention rule, applied at this PR's base).
- Modified device preamble: `csrc/experimental/deepgemm_fp4_gemm/cake_deepgemm_fp4_gemm_device_common.cuh`: relative to `main`, the preamble replaces its 15 inline device helper definitions (`make_warp_uniform`, `elect_sync`, `mbarrier_init`, `mbarrier_wait`, `mbarrier_arrive_expect_tx`, `elect_commit_cg2_multicast`, `desc_encode`, `make_sf_cp_desc_lo_sbo128`, `tcgen05_mma_mxf4_bs_cta2`, `tcgen05_cp_32x128b_warpx4_cta2`, `tma_2d_gmem2smem`, `tma_2d_gmem2smem_cta2`, `tma_3d_gmem2smem_cta2`, `tma_store_2d`, `tmem_ld_x8`) by 15 `#include "cake_device_helpers/..."` lines of the shared helper library, and its header comment adds that translation-unit-local includes (cooperative groups) stay in the kernels that use them (+17 / -141); this is the text this pull request's previous head already carries byte for byte (the file is unchanged relative to the previous head)
- Modified host files: `flashinfer/experimental/deepgemm_fp4_gemm/fp4_gemm.py`. Relative to this pull request's previous head, the device source and binding of the normal BN160 program change (the cross-pass epilogue: a `tcgen05.ld` batch per store pass with one-pass lookahead, the same conversion and store statements); the runtime module changes only by the renamed program record and its `ROUTES` entry; the public API module and the test module are unchanged. No host logic, route rule or public signature changes. The staged update against the previous head changes three delivered files: the kernel and binding of the normal BN160 program, re-emitted under the new content-hashed name `cake_deepgemm_fp4_gemm_b2fa42d3c2801bd3f387` in place of `cake_deepgemm_fp4_gemm_f3546083516a716d0aaa` (the binding changes only by the renamed kernel symbol and the host-shim namespace identifier derived from the new name, `cake_host_shim_53b799869858d4e2` -> `cake_host_shim_fb8ed5f7258c0233`, +8 / -8, no other content; the kernel changes by the renamed symbol and the cross-pass epilogue, +421 / -45 in two hunks), and `fp4_gemm.py` (+15 / -15: the renamed program record and `ROUTES["normal_bm128_bn160_s7"]`, no other content); the other seven programs, the device and host common headers, the package README, the public API module and the test module are byte-identical to the previous head. The update also re-stages the branch on FlashInfer main `22d60b5bb` (the previous head sits on main `3637083a3`, 19 main commits earlier), so a raw head-to-head diff of the two commits also carries those main commits' changes. The test module is FlashInfer main's, unchanged (4 test functions). Added files: `csrc/experimental/deepgemm_fp4_gemm/.clang-format` (the package's clang-format opt-out (`DisableFormat: true`, `SortIncludes: Never`, the same two lines as main's shared `csrc/experimental/.clang-format`); main's #5928 removed this per-package copy when it introduced the shared file, and the exporter re-emits it from its target revision `426d028e1`, which predates #5928, so against main this pull request re-adds a redundant copy; already carried by this pull request's previous head (unchanged relative to it)).

## Per-shape speedup (native DeepGEMM / this revision), cohort native FP4 GEMM rows

The 118-row cohort is the fixed benchmark set of DeepGEMM-family rows this harness tracks on both architectures; its native FP4 GEMM rows are listed here. CUPTI medians of the whole call (every launch of the route), cold L2, the source arm and native DeepGEMM `39d8c4ca` timed back to back in one process (each arm by `bench_gpu_time`, 2 warmup + 10 timed iterations per visit, under the same CUPTI timer; the launcher's three arms -- its control arm (for the six M = 16 / 128 / 512 rows, this row among them: the family's original combined-TMA BM128 / BN128 / 7-stage N128 program, a different program from this row's BN160 program, not that program with the pipeline off; for the two M = 4096 rows, routed at BN256 / BN224, the same kernel family at the row's own tile and stage count with its scale-factor TMA overlap off (for the BN224 row the row's own program with the overlap off; for the BN256 row the launcher's plain BN256 / 6-stage build of the same kernel with the overlap off, without the 8-block large-M tile-order grouping that both the row's own static-shape retrace and the shipped BN256 program carry)), the source arm and native -- are each visited twice in mirrored order (control, source, native, native, source, control), no per-launch interleaving; each reading's per-arm figure is the mean of its two visit medians). The rows this pull request changes against FlashInfer main (8 on B200, 8 on GB300, tagged below) carry these readings: the rows this update re-measured (1 on B200, 1 on GB300) were measured for this change on the head of the acceptance readings itself (the source tree measured before this squash), whose program texts this revision reproduces byte for byte for every native FP4 GEMM row and for the 98 of the 118 cohort rows claimed on the Cake revision named under Producer (identity render of that head against a squash on the same Cake parent as this delivery's squash -- the main head when this delivery was first squashed with the mixed-GEMM export-adapter fix; the later rebuilds of this commit kept that parent -- carried to this revision by construction: its two later formatting-only template fixes touch no program source, and the render also covers the squash parent's move from the measured tree's main base to that parent; the 20 dense-MQA indexer rows are disclosed and not claimed: this change delivers none of their programs; their readings are carried unchanged from the acceptance table of this pull request's previous head (each row keeps the reading of the latest acceptance pass that measured it), and the fp8 and fp4 indexer sources of the Cake revision named under Producer differ from those of every tree those readings were taken on): B200 12 readings per row, one per single-GPU shard, four shards at a time on one node (four distinct GPUs of that node across the twelve shards), on a node whose other four GPUs another user's four-GPU job held throughout the readings (by the cluster's job accounting); GB300 12 readings per row, one per single-GPU shard, four shards at a time on one node (four distinct GPUs of that node across the twelve shards), on a node this acceptance held alone (its 3-seed correctness gate and its sanitizer legs also ran there while the readings were in progress); the other tagged rows keep the readings of the acceptance of this pull request's previous head, carried by program identity; on both architectures each shard pairs that tree's build against native DeepGEMM on its own GPU. One native FP4 GEMM row changes program on both architectures: model-fp4gemm-l2-m512 (the normal BN160 program, `normal_bm128_bn160_s7`); it was re-measured for this update on this revision's head on both architectures. Every other native FP4 GEMM row renders byte-identical to the previous delivery (identity render of the head of the acceptance readings against its Cake parent: the pipeline helpers are in the sources but switched on for the BN160 program only) and keeps the readings of the previous head's acceptance that published it. That identity render reads exactly one changed native FP4 GEMM row per architecture (model-fp4gemm-l2-m512, the normal BN160 program) against its Cake parent, the seven other rows identical (they run six of the seven other programs; the BN16 program serves no cohort row); the row was re-measured on the head on both architectures with 12 readings. Those head readings were taken on the head of the acceptance readings before the Cake squash named under Producer; the identity render of this change against that head (120 / 120 rendered rows per architecture identical: the 118 table rows plus two rendered rows outside the tables) was taken on a squash on the parent of the Cake squash named under Producer (this squash's parent: the main head when this delivery was first squashed with the mixed-GEMM export-adapter fix; the later rebuilds of this commit kept that parent) -- so it also covers the squash parent's move from the measured tree's main base to that parent (15 main commits, among them changes to the Cake code generator) -- and before its two formatting-only template fixes, which touch no program source; after those readings the Cake tree changed, beyond that parent move, only by the mixed-GEMM export-adapter fix (export.py only) and those two template fixes, none of them a file of this family, so the render carries to this commit by construction and the readings carry to the delivered files by program identity. "previous" = the acceptance table from before this pull request's first head (the baseline the previous head's message listed against), measured by the same cohort driver and timing method, not the previous head's own readings; against the previous head itself only model-fp4gemm-l2-m512 moved: B200 7.084 -> 6.912 us (1.0560 -> 1.0852), GB300 6.792 -> 6.636 us (1.0553 -> 1.0801); the seven other rows per architecture repeat the previous head's readings; native DeepGEMM 39d8c4ca is the ratio's arm throughout. "launches" = kernel launches per call, previous -> this revision.

native/source is the median over the readings of the per-reading ratio; the us columns are each arm's own median, so their quotient differs slightly from it.

Summary
Round 2 of the Hopper native BF16 MegaMoE backend (
sm90_bf16_bf16_bf16_push_cake

MoEEpLayer

#4254

#5708

What changed
Combine wire
(the only numerics change; deterministic)
combine_wire="prereduced"
(new): each expert rank pre-reduces, in fp32 (
fmaf
) and in ascending route order, the routes of a token that it computed, rounds once to bf16 and publishes one row per (token, source rank) into the owner's inbox. The owning rank sums the per-rank rows in ascending rank order in fp32 and rounds once. Inbox traffic drops from
T * top_k
rows to
T * world
rows (EP8, top-8: 7.0 to 4.6 rows per token on uniform routing).
combine_wire="prereduced_hilo"
(new): the pre-reduced row plus a bf16 residual row for multi-route groups; a precision-conservative variant kept selectable (it is not faster).
combine_wire="per_route"
: the round-1 wire (one row per route), unchanged and bitwise identical to
feat(cake_mega_moe): SM90 native BF16 MegaMoE expert compute through MoEEpLayer (sm90_bf16_bf16_bf16_push_cake)
#5958
.
Default
(
combine_wire=None

per_route
when the per-rank token capacity is
<= 8

above.

overrides. All ranks must agree; the construction-time allgather rejects mismatches with
MoEEpConfigError
.
Determinism: fixed accumulation order (routes ascending within a rank, ranks ascending across ranks), no fp32 atomics on outputs or partial sums; bitwise run-to-run; eager == CUDA graph.
Protocol fixed-cost levers
(output bit-identical to round 1): publish scratch self-resets instead of four per-round memsets; the pre-reduced worklist is built inside the compact pass (one launch fewer); grid completion counts participating blocks only; compact assigns rows by static grid stride instead of an atomic work queue; publish groups are split across blocks at decode sizes.
Grouped-GEMM epilogue
(sealed sources re-rendered from the generator; output bit-identical): bf16x2 pack, quad transpose and 16-byte stores (FC1+FC2 +4.5 % at T >= 1024; no register or spill change, 168 regs).

atol=rtol=1e-2

Retained concerns
Low · reliability · inferred:
New wire resolution and prerequisite checks run before guarded collective initialization. If only one rank rejects its environment override or fused-tail configuration, that rank exits while peers can wait in the weights-and-buffers collective. This weakens coordinated startup failure containment. The integrated backend bounds the wait by its configured timeout and cleans up locally; bounded recovery for direct runner callers is not established.
Security review details
Security Blast Radius
inferred
— The supported exposure is the participating EP group and layers sharing its matching process-level workspace. The startup failure can affect peers despite originating on one rank. Tenant and service boundaries beyond that group are not established by the supplied deployment evidence.
Security Findings and Attack Paths
inferred
— The supported failure path requires control of rank-local constructor or environment settings and ends in disrupted group initialization. The inspected flow does not establish privilege gain or a cross-tenant write. The canonical security input contains no retained findings, but its coverage remains unknown.
Trust Boundaries and Controls
observed
— The peer-memory protocol relies on rank agreement and trusted layout addresses. New grouping bounds checks abort on invalid metadata, while owner-slot derivation and tagged completion constrain legitimate publishing. These controls are protocol checks, not isolation from a compromised participating rank.
Resilience and Maintainability Implications
observed
— The integrated backend configures an all-rank-consistent initialization timeout and destroys the pipe when runner construction raises. The valid-wire mismatch test specifies coordinated rejection followed by successful construction of a consistent layer; it does not demonstrate recovery from rank-local invalid configuration, and was not executed in this review.
Hardening Proposals
proposed
— Resolve and validate wire prerequisites inside a guarded all-rank initialization phase so a local configuration error is reported before peers enter later collectives. Make direct-caller timeout and cleanup responsibilities explicit.
proposed
— Use the effective resolved wire in workspace identity, or document and enforce immutable environment selection while pooled workspaces remain live. This would make numerical-mode selection and fallback behavior predictable without treating existing self-consistent reuse as a demonstrated isolation defect.

💡 Result:
**PyTorch’s current `main` export generally puts the view offset in `data`, not `byte_offset`.** In `toDLPackImpl`, for non-MPS tensors, `data` is set to `src.const_data_ptr()` or `src.mutable_data_ptr()` and `byte_offset` is set to `0`. For MPS, it instead exports the storage base pointer and sets `byte_offset = storage_offset × element_size`. ([github.com](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/main/aten/src/ATen/DLConvertor.cpp))

So for ordinary CPU/CUDA tensors, a nonzero PyTorch `storage_offset()` is already reflected in the pointer returned by `data_ptr()`; exporting that pointer with `byte_offset = 0` represents the view. MPS uses the alternate base-pointer-plus-offset representation. That distinction follows from the exporter’s assignments; the DLPack header describes `data` as the allocated-data pointer and `byte_offset` as the offset to the beginning of tensor data. ([github.com](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/main/aten/src/ATen/DLConvertor.cpp))

feat(cake_mega_moe): pre-reduced BF16 combine wire and fixed-cost lev…
…
dfc9193
…ers for the SM90 MegaMoE backend

Round 2 of the Hopper native BF16 MegaMoE backend
(`sm90_bf16_bf16_bf16_push_cake`,
flashinfer-ai#5958
). Part of
flashinfer-ai#4254
, follow-up to
flashinfer-ai#5708
.

Combine wire (the only numerics change; deterministic):
- `combine_wire="prereduced"`: each expert rank pre-reduces, in fp32 and in
  ascending route order, the routes of a token that it computed, rounds once
  to bf16 and publishes one row per (token, source rank); the owning rank sums
  the per-rank rows in ascending rank order in fp32 and rounds once. Inbox
  reads drop from T*top_k rows to T*world rows.
- `combine_wire="prereduced_hilo"`: the pre-reduced row plus a bf16 residual
  row for multi-route groups (precision-conservative variant).
- `combine_wire="per_route"`: the round-1 wire (one row per route), unchanged.
- Default (`combine_wire=None`, env unset): `per_route` when the per-rank
  token capacity is <= 8, `prereduced` above. `FLASHINFER_SM90_CAKE_BF16_COMBINE_WIRE`
  overrides; all ranks must agree (verified at construction).
- Fixed accumulation order (routes ascending within a rank, ranks ascending
  across ranks), no fp32 atomics on outputs or partial sums; bitwise
  run-to-run and eager == CUDA graph.

Protocol fixed-cost levers (output bit-identical to round 1): publish scratch
self-resets instead of per-round memsets, the pre-reduced worklist is built
inside the compact pass, grid completion counts participating blocks only,
compact assigns rows by static grid stride, publish groups are split across
blocks at decode sizes.

Grouped-GEMM epilogue (sealed sources re-rendered; output bit-identical):
bf16x2 pack, quad transpose and 16-byte stores.

Measured on one 8xH100 node (CUDA graph, CUPTI, paired same-process A/B
against the round-1 backend, 35 benchmark rows, two independent sessions):
geomean 1.031, 33/35 rows improved (best EP4 T=4096: 1.12); against the split
nccl_ep + CUTLASS BF16 baseline geomean 1.55. Precision against an independent
fp32 reference: aggregate mean-abs and rel-L2 below round 1 on every column;
the atol=rtol=1e-2 test gate is unchanged.

Tests: frozen-sources seal, EP1 (all wires, per-shape default, duplicate-rank
and all-local routing, wire mismatch), EP2/EP4/EP8 torchrun;
`run_tests.sh sm90_bf16_push_cake`. Docs: architecture and runbook updated
(wire semantics, determinism note, benchmark `--combine-wire` flag).

title: [Kernel][Build] Bump DeepGEMM to the 26/09/30 release and adapt the sparse indexer
body:
## Overview

Bump the vendored DeepGEMM pin to the tip of `vllm-project/DeepGEMM` `dev` (`6ce1c5e`): upstream's 26/09/30 public release (vllm-project/DeepGEMM#30, deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM#462) plus vendoring import fixes (vllm-project/DeepGEMM#31, vllm-project/DeepGEMM#32) and a relaxed paged sparse MQA page-stride guard (vllm-project/DeepGEMM#33). Adapt vLLM to the breaking MQA-logits API.

## Claims

- vLLM builds, vendors and imports DeepGEMM 2.8.1.
- The DSA sparse indexer (DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-5.x, GLM-5.3, DeepSeek-V4/V4.1, HY-V4) keeps working on SM90/SM100/SM120 with the new MQA-logits API.
- On SM100 the FP8 indexer cache stays numerically identical: same FP8 values and the same per-token power-of-two scale, now stored as four packed UE8M0 bytes (a valid MXFP8 encoding) because SM100 MQA kernels only take MX scales.

## Breaking changes in DeepGEMM `1e1842a` → `6ce1c5e`

| Change | vLLM impact | Handling |
|---|---|---|
| `deep_gemm/__init__.py` imports a new `deep_gemm/locality_domain.py` | not vendored → `import vllm.third_party.deep_gemm` fails | install it in `deepgemm.cmake` |
| `_C.py` registered the locality-domain shim as `deep_gemm._C.locality_domain` | relative import fails when vendored as `vllm.third_party.deep_gemm`, and vLLM then silently treats DeepGEMM as unavailable | fixed in vllm-project/DeepGEMM#31 (in the pin); `tools/check_wheel_deepgemm.py` now imports the package so CI catches this |
| The C++ MLOPart bridge imported `deep_gemm.utils.mlopart` and the epilogue module was named `deep_gemm.epilogue` | `localize()` (not called by vLLM) would fail when vendored | fixed in vllm-project/DeepGEMM#32 (in the pin): `_C.py` passes its `__package__` to the new `init(library_root_path, python_package_name)` |
| `fp8_fp4_paged_sparse_mqa_logits` page-stride guard lowered from 512 to 256 B (vllm-project/DeepGEMM#33) | DeepSeek-V4.1's sparse-logits block stride stays 512-aligned, which still satisfies it | none |
| `fp8_mqa_logits`, `fp8_paged_mqa_logits`, `fp8_gemm_nt_skip_head_mid`, `get_bf16_mega_gate_config` removed | unused by vLLM | none |
| `clean_logits` / `logits_dtype` removed from `fp8_fp4_(paged_)mqa_logits`; `max_seqlen_k` now required (> 0) | wrapper signatures | `vllm/utils/deep_gemm.py`; prefill chunk metadata carries a host `max_seqlen_k` bound (no device sync) |
| `fp8_fp4_mqa_logits` returns **compressed** logits `[M, max_seqlen_k]` (row `i` starts at K position `ks[i]`) on every arch | prefill top-k / candidate-block / DCP consumers indexed absolute columns | consumers run on row starts `0`, ends `ke - ks`; output indices are unchanged (already relative to `ks`) |
| SM100 MQA kernels take only MXFP8/MXFP4 with packed UE8M0 scales, **BF16 weights**, return **BF16 logits**; paged is varlen-only | FP8 indexer (fp32 per-token scale, scale folded into fp32 weights) rejected | see below |
| `bf16_mega_gate` default `scoring_func` → `'sqrtsoftplus'` | vLLM always passes it | none |
| FP8×FP4 / BF16 Mega MoE assert DeepGEMM's SM count equals the device's | only DBO + DeepEP-HT lowers it (`ubatch_utils.py`), not combined with Mega MoE today | none (noted) |
| Epilogue classes (`epilogue=` kwarg), locality domains, `shutdown` | additive | none |

### SM100 FP8 indexer

Every CUDA FP8 indexer writer already stores an exact power-of-two scale `2^ceil(log2(amax/448))` per 128-wide token. On SM100 (`mqa_logits_use_mx_scales()`) the writers store that scale's exponent as four equal UE8M0 bytes instead of the fp32, which is an exact MXFP8 encoding of the same values (same cache size, same FP8 bytes):

| Writer | Models |
|---|---|
| C++ `indexer_k_quant_and_cache` (`scale_fmt="mxfp8"`) | DeepSeek-V2-class `Indexer` (V3.2 via that class, DeepSeek MTP), HY-V4, DeepSeek-V3.2 under PCP |
| DeepSeek-V3.2 fused norm/RoPE (`_fused_norm_rope_kernel`) | DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-5/5.2 (`GlmMoeDsa`), Dots3Note, V3.2 MTP |
| DeepSeek-V4 compressor (Triton; the CuTeDSL compressor is head-512 MLA only) | DeepSeek-V4 |
| DeepSeek-V4.1 `indexer_k_norm_rope_store` | DeepSeek-V4.1 |
| GLM-5.3 kpool prefill compress + decode update | GLM-5.3 |

Readers need no change: `cp_gather_indexer_k_quant_cache` (prefill, all of the above) and the DCP/PCP gathers copy the 4 scale bytes verbatim, and DeepGEMM reads the paged cache directly. The 512-wide MLA caches, MXFP4 caches, and the MiniMax-M3 / Qwen4 indexers are untouched.

FP8 Q keeps folding its per-(token, head) power-of-two scale into `weights`; `mqa_logits_mx_inputs` passes unit MX Q scales (exact, since `relu(s·x) = s·relu(x)` for `s > 0`) and casts weights to BF16. The BF16 logits are upcast to FP32 for the existing FP32-only top-k kernels (`as_fp32_logits`); routing BF16 logits straight to a BF16-capable top-k (DeepSelect / LiteTopK, #59921/#59922) is a follow-up.

SM90 and SM120 keep the FP8 format, FP32 weights and FP32 logits. Consequently the FP8 indexer cache's scale bytes now differ between SM100 and other architectures: moving that KV cache between SM100 and non-SM100 nodes (cross-generation PD disaggregation, shared KV offload) is not supported for these models. Same-architecture setups are unaffected.

## Validation

All on 4x GB200 (SM100), CUDA 13, torch 2.13; baseline = `main` with the old pin `1e1842a`, same build otherwise.

**GLM-5.3-Flash** (FP8, TP4 + EP, MTP=3, `--max-model-len 131072 --max-num-batched-tokens 131072 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --reasoning-parser glm47`, `reasoning_effort=low`), on the rebased branch vs `main` bfa7e5b7af. MRCR prompts are far longer than the indexer's coverage (2048 pools × 4 = 8K tokens), so they exercise top-k selection; long prefills also engage the TP prefill row sharding from #54951 (confirmed with a temporary log, e.g. 129K-row steps split `[47458, 18791, 42577, 19957]` across ranks):

| | `main` + `1e1842a` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| MRCR, 60 samples of 16K–32K tokens (`tests/evals/mrcr`), match ratio (2 / 4 / 8 needles) | 0.794 (0.823 / 0.798 / 0.760) | 0.810 (0.904 / 0.791 / 0.735) |
| MRCR, 24 samples of 57K–66K tokens, match ratio | 0.578 (4 runs hit max_tokens) | 0.665 |
| GSM8K (1319, 5-shot) | 90.8% | 91.6% |
| Serving, 4 runs of 128 × (4096 in / 512 out) at concurrency 32, output tok/s | 1492 / 1544 / 1491 / 1471 | 1484 / 1476 / 1337 / 1501 |
| Median ITL | 19.85 ms | 19.9 ms |

GLM-5.3 serving throughput tracks the MTP acceptance length, which varies per run (the 1337 tok/s run had 1.31 vs ~1.7–1.8 elsewhere); runs with matching acceptance agree (1476 @ 1.70 vs 1471 @ 1.71).

**DeepSeek-V4-Flash** (before the rebase onto current `main`; baseline 26a488ad93), TP2 + EP, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8 --attention_config.indexer_kv_dtype=fp8`, `--max-model-len 8192`; GSM8K via `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py` (1319 questions, 5-shot, 2 rounds). GSM8K prompts fit inside the indexer's coverage (512 × 4 = 2K tokens), so this checks the SM100 path end to end rather than top-k selection:

| indexer cache | `main` + `1e1842a` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| fp8 | 95.5% / 94.6% | 94.8% / 94.6% |
| mxfp4 | 94.9% | 94.7% |

**Serving** — same server, `vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 4096 --random-output-len 512 --num-prompts 256 --max-concurrency 64 --ignore-eos`, one warm-up + 3 runs each, sequential on the same GPUs:

| | output tok/s | mean TPOT | median ITL |
|---|---|---|---|
| `main` + `1e1842a` | 2968 (2962–2974) | 18.73 ms | 12.80 ms |
| this PR | 2946 (2928–2958) | 18.89 ms | 12.94 ms |

The ~0.8% gap matches the two extra small kernels per indexer layer on SM100 (weights → BF16, row-aware logits → FP32, ~3 µs together). Feeding BF16 straight from the Q producers and into a BF16 top-k removes both.

**Unit tests** (GB200):

```

pytest tests/model_executor/layers/test_mla_short_prefill_indexer.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_*.py tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_indexer_decode_seq_lens.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_glm5next_indexer_block_sizes.py tests/v1/attention/test_kpool_*.py \
  tests/models/glm5next/test_sparse_indexer_topk_dispatch.py tests/v1/cudagraph/test_breakable_cudagraph.py \
  tests/kernels/test_compressor_kv_cache.py tests/kernels/test_fused_indexer_q_rope_quant.py \
  tests/kernels/test_kpool_decode_update_batched.py tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_paged_mxfp4_indexer_plan.py
                                                                               # 558 passed, 35 skipped
pytest tests/kernels/test_fused_deepseek_v32_norm_rope.py                      # 222 passed
pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_deepgemm.py tests/kernels/moe/test_batched_deepgemm.py \
  tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_mega_moe.py tests/kernels/mhc/test_mhc_kernels.py \
  tests/model_executor/test_deep_gemm_warmup.py                                 # all passed

                                                                               # 100 passed, 169 skipped
python tools/check_wheel_deepgemm.py                                           # now also imports the package
```

`tests/kernels/moe/test_silu_mul_fp8_quant_deep_gemm.py` fails on this GB200 with `unspecified launch failure` identically on `main` + `1e1842a` (pre-existing, unrelated). Not run (no hardware): SM90 and SM120; CI's H100 DeepGEMM job covers the SM90 attention tests. CI has no SM100 DeepGEMM job, so the MX path is validated only by the runs above.

**Pin delta `1448881` → `6ce1c5e`**: the end-to-end runs above used `1448881`. The two later commits change no kernel math (vllm-project/DeepGEMM#33 only lowers the host and device stride asserts, vllm-project/DeepGEMM#32 only module naming). Re-checked on `6ce1c5e` on GB200 (the GPUs were shared with another job, so no end-to-end rerun):

```
python tools/check_wheel_deepgemm.py                                           # imports; init takes the package name
pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_deepgemm_attention.py \
  tests/model_executor/layers/test_mla_short_prefill_indexer.py tests/model_executor/test_deep_gemm_warmup.py
                                                                               # 42 passed, 7 skipped (need pip deep_gemm)
pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_deepgemm.py tests/kernels/quantization/test_block_fp8.py -k "deep_gemm or deepgemm"

# 60/60 passed with 64-token pages of 8448 B (MXFP8) / 4352 B (MXFP4), 256- but not 512-aligned
```

## Details

- `tools/build_deepgemm_C.py` now passes `--force` to `setup.py build_ext`. DeepGEMM's `setup.py` lists only `csrc/python_api.cpp`, so after a pin change that touched only headers (`config.hpp` in vllm-project/DeepGEMM#32) an incremental build silently kept the old extension and the import failed with `deep_gemm::init() expected at most 1 argument(s)`. CMake already reruns this step on DeepGEMM header changes and `python_api.cpp` is the only translation unit, so forcing adds no work.
- Why not duplicate: no open PR bumps DeepGEMM past `1e1842a` or adapts the indexer to the new MQA API (#59503 bumps to an older SM107 fix already contained in the current pin; #59482 is the Stable ABI migration).
- AI assistance (Claude Code) was used; the submitter reviewed every changed line and ran the tests below.

title: [ROCm][Perf][Attention] Reduce temporary allocations in sparse-indexer prefill
body: Reuse the freshly produced [H, M, N] score buffer for scaling, ReLU and head weighting in fp8_mqa_logits_torch, then mask the reduced logits in place, instead of allocating separate full-size FP32 temporaries. Inputs, FP32 operation order and the head reduction are unchanged. Targets the unpaged Torch prefill fallback.On RX 7900 XTX this cuts function wall time by 6.4–6.5% and incremental peak allocated memory by ~48% for prefill shapes (256, 576) and (256, 768). Outputs are byte-identical to baseline.

title: [Bug]: SM120 CUTLASS blockwise FP8 GEMM rejects N % 128 != 0 (Invalid status; kv_a_proj N=576 in DeepSeek shapes)
body:
### Your current environment

RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120), CUDA 13.0, torch 2.11.0+cu130, current main (f7fc0ca99) with the precompiled nightly kernels.

### Describe the bug

The SM120 CUTLASS c3x blockwise FP8 GEMM (`scaled_mm_blockwise_sm120_fp8.cu`) rejects every problem whose weight output dim N is not a multiple of 128, failing with `cutlass_gemm_caller, .../cutlass_gemm_caller.cuh:52, Invalid status` (CUTLASS `can_implement` fails). All three tile configs in `scaled_mm_blockwise_sm120_fp8_dispatch.cuh` (default 128x128x128, pingpong 64x128x128, swap-ab 128x32x128) reject these shapes, so it is not M-range dependent.

Sweep on the RTX PRO 6000 with fp32 scales, via `ops.cutlass_scaled_mm` exactly as `CutlassFp8BlockScaledMMKernel.apply_block_scaled_mm` calls it (M in {1,16,32,64,83,128,256,512} x K in {1024, 7168}):

| N | result |
|---|---|
| 512, 1536, 7168 | OK at every M/K (max rel err 2-3e-3 vs fp32 dequant reference = bf16 rounding) |
| 576, 2112 | `Invalid status` at every M/K |

N=576 is `kv_a_proj_with_mqa` (512+64) in DeepSeek V3-family models, so any block-FP8 DeepSeek-shaped checkpoint hits this on SM120 once it routes to the CUTLASS kernel. The existing test `tests/kernels/quantization/test_block_fp8.py::test_w8a8_block_fp8_cutlass_matmul` (M=32, N=576, K=7168) fails on SM120 today with exactly this error, while the same test passes on SM90 CI - the alignment requirement is specific to the SM120 kernel.

#47988 makes `CutlassFp8BlockScaledMMKernel.can_implement` decline unaligned-N layers on SM12x so kernel selection falls through to Triton, which serves them correctly. That is a selection-level workaround; the kernel-level gap remains and is worth fixing in the dispatch (e.g. a compatible epilogue/tile config for ragged N, or padding), at which point the `can_implement` guard can be relaxed.

Related: #47818 (SM120 block-FP8 dispatch crash for ue8m0 scales, same code path); #40016 is the same failure class on SM90 for the M dim (swap_ab, non-multiple-of-4 M).

title: Add DeepSeek-V4 XPU support with FP8 KV cache
body:
## [XPU] Add DeepSeek-V4 XPU support

### Summary

This PR enables DeepSeek-V4-Flash to run on Intel XPU with functional correctness. The model uses FP8 KV cache (same as CUDA path) and routes XPU-incompatible operations to PyTorch/Triton fallbacks.

**Validated**: GSM8k 50 samples TP=4, **98% strict-match**.

### Changes

#### Attention (`deepseek_v4_attention.py`, `sparse_attn_indexer.py`)

- Add XPU decode path (`_forward_decode_xpu`) that dequants FP8 paged cache to bf16 then runs Triton sparse MLA
- Route indexer ops (`indexer_k_quant_and_cache`, `cp_gather_indexer_k_quant_cache`, `fp8_mqa_logits`, `fp8_paged_mqa_logits`) to PyTorch implementations in `_xpu_ops.py`
- Add `forward_xpu` for MHC Pre/Post/Fuse (calls `mhc_pre_torch`/`mhc_post_torch` — no tilelang on XPU)
- Skip FlashMLA tile_scheduler_metadata build on XPU (not used)
- Disable aux_stream parallelism on XPU (no overlap benefit)

#### New Triton kernels (3 files)

| File | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `xpu_qnorm_rope_kv_fp8_insert.py` | Fused QNorm + RoPE + KV cache insert for SWA compressor |
| `xpu_sparse_decode_fp8.py` | Sparse decode: dequant FP8 pages → bf16 → Triton attention |
| `xpu_sparse_mla_bf16.py` | C4A sparse prefill over contiguous bf16 KV workspace |

#### Quantization (`scaled_mm/triton.py`, `linear/__init__.py`, `input_quant_fp8.py`, `fp8_utils.py`)

- Register `TritonFp8BlockScaledMMKernel` for XPU platform (FP8 block-scaled GEMM via Triton)
- Dynamic group quant: route to `torch.ops.vllm.triton_per_token_group_quant_fp8` custom op (avoids torch.compile trying to trace FP8 Triton internals)
- Upcast E8M0 block scales to fp32 on XPU (same as ROCm path)

#### MoE routing (`fused_topk_bias_router.py`)

- Add `_topk_softplus_sqrt_torch`: pure PyTorch fallback for `topk_softplus_sqrt` scoring on XPU/CPU
- Key fix: bias is used for expert **selection** only, not for weight computation (prevents near-uniform routing weights)

#### Platform compatibility (misc)

- `SiluAndMulWithClamp`: XPU uses `forward_native` (no `_C.silu_and_mul_with_clamp` op)
- `fused_inv_rope_fp8_quant`: skip `launch_pdl` kwarg on XPU
- `rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py`: replace `"cuda"` device literals with `q.device`; replace `.is_cuda` asserts with `not .is_cpu`
- `deepseek_v4.py`: XPU reuses ROCm forward path (sequential execution, no aux streams)
- `deepseek_compressor.py`: minor guard fix

#### `_xpu_ops.py` (+260 lines)

- `cp_gather_indexer_k_quant_cache`: rewritten to handle BLOCK-PACKED cache layout with `as_strided` flat byte view
- `fp8_mqa_logits`: prefill indexer logits via einsum (bf16 dequant → score → relu → weight)
- `fp8_paged_mqa_logits`: decode indexer logits with paged FP8 cache (block-table lookup + dequant)
- `indexer_k_quant_and_cache`: FP8 quantize + cache insert

### Known limitations / future work

- **MoE**: `_topk_softplus_sqrt_torch` is a PyTorch loop fallback; needs SYCL/Triton fused kernel
- **Indexer logits**: pure PyTorch einsum; needs dedicated SYCL MQA kernel for performance
- **FP8 MLA sparse attention**: decode dequants entire pages to bf16 before Triton; native FP8 paged attention would eliminate this copy
- **MHC**: using `mhc_pre_torch`/`mhc_post_torch` (no Triton fusion yet)
- **top_k**: using `torch.topk`; SYCL specialized kernel needed for decode

diff --git a/vllm/model_executor/kernels/attention/dsa/candidate_paged_logits.py b/vllm/model_executor/kernels/attention/dsa/candidate_paged_logits.py
new file mode 100644
index 000000000000..26e543003596
--- /dev/null
+++ b/vllm/model_executor/kernels/attention/dsa/candidate_paged_logits.py
@@ -0,0 +1,502 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""SM90 candidate-only decode scoring for the DeepSeek V4.1 two-level indexer.
+
+The V4.1 indexer publishes candidate blocks at ``candidate_source_layer_id``;
+the later consumer indexers are meant to select their top-k *inside those
+candidate blocks only*. On SM100 that is DeepGEMM's sparse MQA-logits kernels.
+SM90 has no equivalent, so the consumers score the whole compressed context
+with the dense paged kernel and then mask the logits down to the candidate
+blocks, discarding the work outside them. With a 16K-position candidate set
+against a 1M-position context that is ~98% of the scoring.
+
+This module scores only the candidate positions, reading K **in place** from
+the paged FP8 indexer cache. Logits land in a compact ``[rows, num_cands *
+candidate_block_size]`` buffer whose columns are candidate-relative, the usual
+decode top-k runs over that buffer, and the selected columns are remapped back
+to request-local compressed positions.
+
+Two properties keep replays correct under full CUDA-graph capture:
+
+* **No per-step host decision.** Context lengths stay on the device; the host
+  only sees shapes that are fixed by the model and scheduler config. A full
+  CUDA graph therefore cannot bake a context-dependent choice, and replays
+  stay correct at any live context length.
+* **K is read in place.** Unlike a scheme that gathers candidate K into a
+  scratch buffer first, no K data is copied that the dense path would not
+  also read. The only extra work is per-row candidate bookkeeping (expansion
+  and sorting of block ids), index arithmetic paid only while the path is
+  active.
+
+Numerics follow the decode reference (``fp8_paged_mqa_logits``): dot, relu,
+head weights, sum over heads, then one dequantization multiply per column.
+Scaling after the relu is exact because the per-position scale is positive,
+and it costs ``num_heads`` times fewer multiplies.
+"""
+
+import torch
+
+from vllm.logger import init_logger
+from vllm.model_executor.kernels.attention.dsa.sparse_mqa_logits import (
+    _sparse_topk_remap_kernel,
+    candidate_blocks_to_sparse_indices,
+)
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.indexer_topk import (
+    RADIX_TOPK_WORKSPACE_SIZE,
+    get_indexer_topk,
+)
+from vllm.triton_utils import tl, triton
+from vllm.v1.worker.workspace import current_workspace_manager
+
+logger = init_logger(__name__)
+
+# One fp32 scale per cached position, stored after the block's value bytes.
+INDEXER_SCALE_BYTES = 4
+# The same value for use inside the kernel; Triton only reads globals that are
+# instantiated as constexpr.
+_SCALE_BYTES = tl.constexpr(4)
+
+# Compact columns per program. A multiple of the candidate block size, and at
+# least 16 so the MMA has a full M tile.
+_BLOCK_N = 128
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _prepare_candidate_rows_kernel(
+    seq_lens,
+    row_ks,
+    row_ends,
+    rows,
+    next_n: tl.constexpr,
+    per_row_lens: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    """Per-row causal context length, and the zero K-range start the paged
+    candidate expansion expects (its block ids are context-relative)."""
+    offsets = tl.program_id(0) * BLOCK + tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
+    mask = offsets < rows
+    if per_row_lens:
+        lens = tl.load(seq_lens + offsets, mask=mask, other=0)
+    else:
+        # One length per request: speculative row ``s`` of a request sees
+        # ``next_n - 1 - s`` fewer positions than the request's newest row.
+        request = offsets // next_n
+        step = offsets % next_n
+        base = tl.load(seq_lens + request, mask=mask, other=0)
+        lens = tl.maximum(base - next_n + 1 + step, 0)
+    tl.store(row_ks + offsets, 0, mask=mask)
+    tl.store(row_ends + offsets, lens, mask=mask)
+
+
+@triton.jit(
+    # ``cache_block_stride`` and ``cache_block_size`` are deliberately left
+    # specializable: Triton needs their divisibility to prove that a
+    # position's value bytes are 16-byte aligned and emit vector loads for the
+    # candidate gather. Hiding it costs roughly 20x on the K stream.
+    do_not_specialize=[
+        "num_blocks",
+        "bt_width",
+        "width",
+        "bt_row_repeat",
+    ]
+)
+def _paged_candidate_logits_kernel(
+    q_ptr,  # fp8 [rows, H, D]
+    kv_bytes,  # uint8 flat storage view of the paged indexer cache
+    kv_scales,  # fp32 reinterpretation of the same flat storage
+    w_ptr,  # fp32 [rows, H]
+    blocks_ptr,  # int32 [rows, S] candidate block ids, sorted, padded tail
+    end_ptr,  # int32 [rows] valid compact column count
+    causal_ptr,  # int32 [rows] causal context length, compressed positions
+    bt_ptr,  # int32 [bt_rows, P] page table
+    out_ptr,  # fp32 [rows, width]
+    stride_q_row,
+    stride_q_head,
+    stride_w_row,
+    stride_blocks_row,
+    stride_bt_row,
+    stride_bt_col,
+    stride_out_row,
+    bt_row_repeat,
+    cache_block_stride,  # bytes per physical cache block
+    cache_block_size,  # positions per cache block
+    num_blocks,
+    bt_width,
+    width,
+    H: tl.constexpr,  # indexer heads actually present
+    H_PAD: tl.constexpr,  # padded to a power of two for the MMA
+    D: tl.constexpr,  # indexer head dim
+    CBS: tl.constexpr,  # positions per candidate block
+    BLOCK_N: tl.constexpr,  # compact columns per program
+):
+    """Score one tile of candidate columns for one decode row.
+
+    Compact column ``c`` scores request-local compressed position
+    ``blocks[row, c // CBS] * CBS + c % CBS``. Columns past the row's valid
+    candidate prefix, columns whose block is padding, and columns past the
+    row's causal length all become ``-inf`` so the top-k never selects them.
+    """
+    row = tl.program_id(0).to(tl.int64)
+    cols = tl.program_id(1) * BLOCK_N + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_N)
+    in_bounds = cols < width
+
+    end = tl.load(end_ptr + row)
+    causal = tl.load(causal_ptr + row)
+    live = in_bounds & (cols < end)
+
+    blk = tl.load(
+        blocks_ptr + row * stride_blocks_row + cols // CBS, mask=live, other=-1
+    ).to(tl.int64)
+    pos = blk * CBS + cols % CBS
+    # The expansion pads the tail with a repeat of the largest block, so the
+    # causal bound is what rejects those columns.
+    live = live & (blk >= 0) & (pos < causal)
+
+    page = tl.where(live, pos // cache_block_size, 0)
+    live = live & (page < bt_width)
+    phys = tl.load(
+        bt_ptr + (row // bt_row_repeat) * stride_bt_row + page * stride_bt_col,
+        mask=live,
+        other=-1,
+    ).to(tl.int64)
+    live = live & (phys >= 0) & (phys < num_blocks)
+    safe_phys = tl.where(live, phys, 0)
+    page_off = tl.where(live, pos % cache_block_size, 0)
+
+    d = tl.arange(0, D)
+    h = tl.arange(0, H_PAD)
+    h_live = h < H
+
+    # Values are contiguous per position, so a column's D bytes are one
+    # coalesced segment and consecutive columns of a candidate block adjoin.
+    k_offset = safe_phys * cache_block_stride + page_off * D
+    k_block = tl.load(
+        kv_bytes + k_offset[:, None] + d[None, :],
+        mask=live[:, None],
+        other=0,
+    ).to(tl.float8e4nv, bitcast=True)
+    # Zero-padded heads contribute relu(0) * 0 = 0, so the padding is exact.
+    # Loaded as the MMA's K-major operand directly; the tile is small and this
+    # avoids an in-kernel transpose of an fp8 operand.
+    q_block = tl.load(
+        q_ptr + row * stride_q_row + h[None, :] * stride_q_head + d[:, None],
+        mask=h_live[None, :],
+        other=0.0,
+    )
+    weights = tl.load(w_ptr + row * stride_w_row + h, mask=h_live, other=0.0).to(
+        tl.float32
+    )
+
+    # [BLOCK_N, H_PAD] on fp8 tensor cores with fp32 accumulation. Scoring the
+    # columns as the MMA's M dimension keeps the large operand untransposed.
+    scores = tl.dot(k_block, q_block)
+    scores = tl.maximum(scores, 0.0)
+    scores = scores * weights[None, :]
+    acc = tl.sum(scores, axis=1)
+
+    # Scales follow the block's value bytes, one fp32 per position.
+    sc_idx = (
+        (safe_phys * cache_block_stride) // _SCALE_BYTES
+        + (cache_block_size * D) // _SCALE_BYTES
+        + page_off
+    )
+    acc = acc * tl.load(kv_scales + sc_idx, mask=live, other=0.0)
+
+    tl.store(
+        out_ptr + row * stride_out_row + cols,
+        tl.where(live, acc, -float("inf")),
+        mask=in_bounds,
+    )
+
+
+def _flat_cache_views(
+    kv_cache: torch.Tensor, head_dim: int
+) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    """Zero-copy ``(uint8, fp32)`` one-dimensional views of the cache storage.
+
+    Packed KV-cache views leave gaps between logical pages, because other
+    layers share the same physical manager block, so ``view(-1)`` is invalid.
+    Span the gaps instead and let the kernel use the physical block stride.
+    """
+    cache_block_size = kv_cache.shape[1]
+    page_bytes = cache_block_size * (head_dim + INDEXER_SCALE_BYTES)
+    assert kv_cache.dtype == torch.uint8 and kv_cache.ndim == 3
+    assert kv_cache.shape[2] == head_dim + INDEXER_SCALE_BYTES, (
+        "FP8 indexer cache entry must be head_dim+4 bytes, got shape "
+        f"{tuple(kv_cache.shape)} with head_dim={head_dim}"
+    )
+    assert kv_cache.stride(2) == 1 and kv_cache.stride(0) >= page_bytes
+    assert kv_cache.storage_offset() % INDEXER_SCALE_BYTES == 0
+    assert kv_cache.stride(0) % INDEXER_SCALE_BYTES == 0
+    storage_span = (kv_cache.shape[0] - 1) * kv_cache.stride(0) + page_bytes
+    assert storage_span % INDEXER_SCALE_BYTES == 0
+    kv_bytes = torch.as_strided(kv_cache, (storage_span,), (1,))
+    return kv_bytes, kv_bytes.view(torch.float32)
+
+
+def paged_candidate_logits(
+    q: torch.Tensor,
+    kv_cache: torch.Tensor,
+    weights: torch.Tensor,
+    candidate_blocks: torch.Tensor,
+    end: torch.Tensor,
+    causal_lens: torch.Tensor,
+    block_table: torch.Tensor,
+    candidate_block_size: int,
+    head_dim: int,
+    out: torch.Tensor,
+) -> None:
+    """Score each row's candidate positions into a compact logits buffer.
+
+    Args:
+        q: [rows, H, D] fp8 queries. On the SM90 FP8 path the per-token scale
+            is already folded into ``weights``.
+        kv_cache: [num_blocks, block_size, head_dim + 4] uint8 paged indexer
+            cache; per block, all value bytes then all fp32 scales.
+        weights: [rows, H] per-head weights.
+        candidate_blocks: [rows, S] int32 candidate block ids, sorted with a
+            padded tail, as produced by ``candidate_blocks_to_sparse_indices``.
+        end: [rows] int32 valid compact column count per row.
+        causal_lens: [rows] int32 causal context length in compressed
+            positions.
+        block_table: [bt_rows, P] int32 page table; ``rows`` must be a whole
+            multiple of ``bt_rows`` for speculative row expansion.
+        candidate_block_size: Compressed positions per candidate block.
+        head_dim: Indexer head dim.
+        out: [rows, S * candidate_block_size] fp32 output.
+
+    """
+    rows, width = out.shape
+    num_heads = q.shape[1]
+    assert q.shape[0] == rows and weights.shape == (rows, num_heads)
+    assert q.shape[2] == head_dim
+    assert out.dtype == torch.float32 and out.stride(1) == 1
+    assert candidate_blocks.shape[0] == rows
+    assert candidate_blocks.shape[1] * candidate_block_size == width
+    assert candidate_blocks.dtype == torch.int32
+    assert end.dtype == torch.int32 and causal_lens.dtype == torch.int32
+    assert block_table.dtype == torch.int32 and block_table.ndim == 2
+    assert rows % block_table.shape[0] == 0
+    assert q.stride(2) == 1
+
+    kv_bytes, kv_scales = _flat_cache_views(kv_cache, head_dim)
+    block_n = max(_BLOCK_N, candidate_block_size)
+    assert block_n % candidate_block_size == 0
+    _paged_candidate_logits_kernel[(rows, triton.cdiv(width, block_n))](
+        q,
+        kv_bytes,
+        kv_scales,
+        weights,
+        candidate_blocks,
+        end,
+        causal_lens,
+        block_table,
+        out,
+        q.stride(0),
+        q.stride(1),
+        weights.stride(0),
+        candidate_blocks.stride(0),
+        block_table.stride(0),
+        block_table.stride(1),
+        out.stride(0),
+        rows // block_table.shape[0],
+        kv_cache.stride(0),
+        kv_cache.shape[1],
+        kv_cache.shape[0],
+        block_table.shape[1],
+        width,
+        H=num_heads,
+        H_PAD=triton.next_power_of_2(num_heads),
+        D=head_dim,
+        CBS=candidate_block_size,
+        BLOCK_N=block_n,
+    )
+
+
+def candidate_paged_workspace_specs(
+    rows: int,
+    num_candidates: int,
+    candidate_block_size: int,
+    topk_tokens: int,
+) -> list[tuple[tuple[int, ...], torch.dtype]]:
+    """Simultaneously-live scratch for candidate-only decode scoring.
+
+    The radix reservation must stay first: nested cooperative/persistent top-k
+    requests the same workspace prefix while the remaining buffers are live.
+    """
+    width = num_candidates * candidate_block_size
+    return [
+        ((RADIX_TOPK_WORKSPACE_SIZE,), torch.uint8),
+        ((rows,), torch.int32),  # row_ks
+        ((rows,), torch.int32),  # causal lens, then candidate-column ends
+        ((rows, num_candidates), torch.int32),  # sorted candidate block ids
+        ((rows,), torch.int32),  # valid compact columns per row
+        ((rows, width), torch.float32),  # compact logits
+        ((rows, topk_tokens), torch.int32),  # compact top-k columns
+    ]
+
+
+def candidate_paged_score_decode(
+    q: torch.Tensor,
+    kv_cache: torch.Tensor,
+    weights: torch.Tensor,
+    seq_lens: torch.Tensor,
+    block_table: torch.Tensor,
+    candidate_blocks: torch.Tensor,
+    candidate_block_size: int,
+    next_n: int,
+    topk_tokens: int,
+    topk_backend: str,
+    topk_indices: torch.Tensor,
+    head_dim: int,
+) -> None:
+    """Select each decode row's top-k inside its candidate blocks.
+
+    Writes request-local compressed positions into ``topk_indices``, ``-1``
+    padded, matching what the dense score-then-mask path produces.
+
+    Args:
+        q: [rows, H, D] fp8 queries in the padded decode layout
+            ``[B, next_n]`` flattened.
+        kv_cache: [num_blocks, block_size, head_dim + 4] uint8 indexer cache.
+        weights: [rows, H] per-head weights with the Q scale folded in.
+        seq_lens: [B, next_n] or [B, 1] int32 causal context lengths.
+        block_table: [B, P] int32 page table.
+        candidate_blocks: [B or rows, S] int32 request-local candidate block
+            ids, ``-1`` padded, unsorted.
+        candidate_block_size: Compressed positions per candidate block.
+        next_n: Query rows per request in the padded layout.
+        topk_tokens: Positions to keep per row.
+        topk_backend: Decode top-k backend, see ``get_indexer_topk``.
+        topk_indices: [rows, topk_tokens] int32 output.
+        head_dim: Indexer head dim.
+
+    """
+    rows = q.shape[0]
+    num_candidates = candidate_blocks.shape[1]
+    width = num_candidates * candidate_block_size
+    # The candidate buffer is indexed per decode row, like the logits the
+    # dense path masks, and may be a longer buffer view than this step needs.
+    # It can also hold one row per request, in which case the expansion
+    # repeats each request's candidates over its speculative rows.
+    # Candidates are indexed per decode row, matching the dense path's mask
+    # (``candidates + row * stride_row``); only the causal lengths are shared
+    # across a request's speculative rows. The buffer is sized for
+    # max_num_batched_tokens, so it is usually longer than this step needs.
+    assert candidate_blocks.shape[0] >= rows, (candidate_blocks.shape[0], rows)
+    candidate_blocks = candidate_blocks[:rows]
+
+    (
+        _radix_reserve,
+        row_ks,
+        causal_lens,
+        sorted_blocks,
+        end,
+        logits,
+        local_topk,
+    ) = current_workspace_manager().get_simultaneous(
+        *candidate_paged_workspace_specs(
+            rows, num_candidates, candidate_block_size, topk_tokens
+        )
+    )
+
+    _prepare_candidate_rows_kernel[(triton.cdiv(rows, 128),)](
+        seq_lens,
+        row_ks,
+        causal_lens,
+        rows,
+        next_n=next_n,
+        per_row_lens=seq_lens.numel() == rows,
+        BLOCK=128,
+    )
+    # Sorting the candidate ids makes the valid columns a prefix, which is
+    # what the top-k backends' per-row bounds require. ``end`` accounts for a
+    # partial final block.
+    candidate_blocks_to_sparse_indices(
+        candidate_blocks,
+        row_ks,
+        causal_lens,
+        candidate_block_size,
+        candidate_block_size,
+        out=(sorted_blocks, end),
+    )
+    paged_candidate_logits(
+        q,
+        kv_cache,
+        weights,
+        sorted_blocks,
+        end,
+        causal_lens,
+        block_table,
+        candidate_block_size,
+        head_dim,
+        logits,
+    )
+    # ``width`` is fixed by the model config, so passing it as the host-side
+    # bound keeps this call free of any context-dependent value and therefore
+    # safe to capture in a CUDA graph.
+    get_indexer_topk(topk_backend)(
+        logits,
+        end.view(-1, next_n),
+        next_n,
+        local_topk,
+        topk_tokens,
+        width,
+    )
+    _sparse_topk_remap_kernel[(rows,)](
+        local_topk,
+        local_topk.stride(0),
+        sorted_blocks,
+        sorted_blocks.stride(0),
+        row_ks,
+        row_ks.stride(0),
+        topk_indices,
+        topk_indices.stride(0),
+        topk_tokens,
+        width,
+        SBK=candidate_block_size,
+        K_POW2=triton.next_power_of_2(topk_tokens),
+    )
+
+
+def candidate_paged_decode_available(
+    use_fp4_cache: bool,
+    dcp_world_size: int,
+    use_pcp: bool,
+    candidate_block_size: int,
+    num_candidates: int,
+    topk_tokens: int,
+    head_dim: int,
+) -> bool:
+    """Whether candidate-only decode scoring applies to this configuration.
+
+    Every input is fixed by the model, platform and scheduler config, so the
+    answer is a CUDA-graph invariant: a captured graph cannot diverge from the
+    path chosen while it was captured.
+
+    Restricted to SM90 with the FP8 indexer cache and no context parallelism.
+    SM100 has the native sparse kernels, and the other platforms keep the
+    dense score-then-mask fallback.
+    """
+    import vllm.envs as envs
+    from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+
+    if not envs.VLLM_DSA_CANDIDATE_PAGED_DECODE:
+        return False
+    if not (
+        current_platform.is_cuda() and current_platform.is_device_capability_family(90)
+    ):
+        return False
+    if use_fp4_cache or dcp_world_size != 1 or use_pcp:
+        return False
+    if num_candidates <= 0 or num_candidates & (num_candidates - 1):
+        # The candidate expansion's in-register sort needs a power of two.
+        return False
+    if candidate_block_size <= 0 or candidate_block_size & (candidate_block_size - 1):
+        # Compact columns are indexed by shifting, and the MMA tile must be a
+        # whole number of candidate blocks.
+        return False
+    if topk_tokens > num_candidates * candidate_block_size:
+        return False
+    # The MMA's K dimension is the head dim.
+    return head_dim > 0 and not (head_dim & (head_dim - 1))

From: yeshihai <71063616+yeshihai@users.noreply.github.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 11:48:16 +0800
Subject: [PATCH 2/3] Share the per-step candidate plan across consumer layers

The candidate expansion (prepare + sort) is a deterministic function of the
step-level candidate buffer and seq_lens, identical for every
candidate-consuming layer, but it ran once per layer. Compute it once per
step into builder-owned buffers and let the later layers reuse it, the same
pattern the SM100 path uses for its kernel metadata. Bit-identical
memoization: same input tensors, same kernels, same output.

Also early-exit scoring tiles fully past a row's valid candidate count, so
short contexts no longer pay MMA work for the padded tail of the fixed-width
candidate window. The grid stays static, so this is CUDA-graph safe.

Signed-off-by: yeshihai <71063616+yeshihai@users.noreply.github.com>

From c7509a10e5740befa3eaa6d12f73cd7d88db6c92 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001

Subject: [PATCH 3/3] Extend the bandwidth guard to the shared-plan path

The production path scores with a plan prepared once per step, whose buffers
come from the builder rather than the workspace arena. A different stride or
alignment proof would slow the gather without failing any correctness test,
so pin the bandwidth floor on both modes.
